key_insight: A fixed, residual-triggered ansatz schedule can outperform adaptive operator screening for variational imaginary-time evolution on non-integrable systems.
engineering_relevance: Avoiding repeated operator-pool screening and global parameter re-optimization can reduce circuit costs for ground-state estimation.
method: Predefine layers using nested Hamiltonian commutators, grouped by symmetry and particle number.
Append the next layer when the relative McLachlan residual exceeds a threshold.
Evolve parameters through variational imaginary-time updates without adaptive pool screening.
evidence_signal: Across five non-integrable Ising and stretched-H₄ systems, the method reached 10⁻⁴ relative error using 1.6–5.4× fewer circuits than the cheapest adaptive comparator; the chain advantage persisted from 8 to 16 sites.
watch_item: The advantage disappears for transverse-field Ising models, at 10⁻⁶ relative-error targets, and when weak layers are scheduled too early.
paper_title: Pool-free, residual-triggered ansatz growth for variational imaginary-time evolution: when a fixed operator order beats adaptive screening
